texts.preamble: Satish Kumar vs Department Of P.F.A on 22 November, 2022 In The Court Of Sh. Harjyot Singh Bhalla Additional Sessions Judge-04, Patiala House Courts, New Delhi Criminal Appeal No. 8635/2016 Cnr No. Dlnd01-001640-2016 Cc No. 172/2000 Deepak Kumar S/o Sh. Ram Dutt Sharma M/s Deepak Milk Centre, Shop No. 1/11701, Panchsheel Garden, Naveen Shahdra, Delhi Satish Kumar S/o Sh. Mala Ram M/s Deepak Milk Centre, Shop No. 1/11701, Panchsheel Garden, Naveen Shahdra, Delhi ...Appellants Versus Department Of P.F.A Govt. of Nct of Delhi Nct Of Delhi New Delhi ...Respondents Date of Institution : 13.01.2016 Date of decision : 22.11.2022 Cr Appeal No. 8635/2016 Page 1 of 8 Judgment
texts.facts: 3. The brief allegations in the present case are that the officials from the Department had heard about synthetic milk being sold in the trans-Yamuna area and accordingly, they raided M/s Deepak Milk Centre at Naveen Shahdra, Delhi at around 06:00 PM on 22.12.1999. 4. When they disclosed their identity and purpose of visiting the said shop, the milk stored in the stainless steel jar was thrown on the ground by an employee Satish Kumar at the instance of Deepak Kumar, the proprietor of the shop. 5. Immediately, a sample of the spilled milk was taken by the Food Inspector and the stainless steel container was also seized. Police was called and ultimately an FIR also came to be registered under Section 186/353/34 IPC for preventing the Food Inspector from performing his duty and taking a sample. 6. The sample so lifted from the ground was never sent to the PA for examination. However, one more sample of milk was lifted from another drum lying in the shop and that sample conforms to the standards laid down and, therefore, prosecution in the present case was lodged only u/s 16(1)(c) and (d) of PFA as a complaint case and a charge-sheet was filed for offence u/s 186/353/34 of IPC on the FIR. Ultimately, both cases were clubbed and tried together and a common judgment passed. 7. Although, I have noticed that there are several contradictions in the testimony of the witnesses viz-a-viz the place where the drum was lying at the time when the sample was proposed to be taken, as also, viz-a-viz who had thrown the milk and the manner in which the milk was lifted from the ground and placed in the bottle, however, it needs to be seen that witnesses in the present case were examined 10 years after the alleged incident and over the passage of time minor contradictions are bound to arise in the testimony of the witnesses. 8. Further, there is no complaint placed on record on behalf of the accused persons that a false case was registered against them on the pretext that they had thrown the milk, whereas in the evidence, it was being suggested to the witnesses that when the milk vendor tried to lift the Can/drum from the premises, he was stopped by the PFA Staff and in the said process the said utensil had fallen on the ground. Further, the accused persons had neither appeared as defence witnesses and examined themselves to depose that the milk had fallen due to an accident and not intentionally spilled nor the said alleged milk vendor was produced as a defence witness, although, only a suggestion was given to PW-3 in this regard.
